theory_refs.why: Why a window cannot work here.
The bottleneck that becomes a lookup.
Avoid counting empty subarrays when k = 0.

stages.title: Understand
stages.body:
✍️ f(array of ints, possibly negative; k) → number of contiguous subarrays whose sum is exactly k.
- n ≤ 2·10⁴, values in [−1000, 1000], k in [−10⁷, 10⁷].
- [1, 1, 1], k = 2 → 2. [1, 2, 3], k = 3 → 2 ([1,2] and [3]).

stages.title: Analyse
stages.body:
✍️ "Subarray sum" + negatives → not a window. "Count" + "exactly k" → think prefix sums.
✍️ By hand: sum(i..j) = pre[j+1] − pre[i]. For a fixed end, I want starts whose prefix equals (current prefix − k).
✍️ Hard part: counting **all** such starts quickly, and not missing subarrays that start at 0.
✍️ Edges: k = 0; negative values; a single element equal to k.

stages.title: Brainstorm: brute → optimal
stages.body:
✍️ **1. Brute.** All (i, j) with an inner sum loop. O(n³).
✍️ **2. Better.** Fix i, extend j with a running sum. O(n²) — 4·10⁸, too slow in practice.
✍️ ↳ Bottleneck: for each end, trying every start.
✍️ ↳ Job description: "count earlier prefix sums equal to run − k". Unlock: searching for a known value → store prefix sums in a map with their counts.
✍️ **3. Optimal.** One pass; `cnt[prefix] = how many times seen`; add cnt[run − k] at each step. O(n) time, O(n) space.

stages.title: Algorithm in words
stages.body:
✍️ 1. Keep a running prefix sum, starting at 0, and a map of prefix counts containing {0: 1}.
✍️ 2. For each element, add it to the running sum.
✍️ 3. Add the number of earlier prefixes equal to (running − k) to the answer.
✍️ 4. Record the current running sum in the map.

stages.title: Pseudocode
stages.body:
```
STATE   cnt = map {0: 1}; run = 0; ans = 0
LOOP    for x in a
UPDATE    run += x
CHECK     ans += cnt[run - k]        (query first, using find)
UPDATE    cnt[run] += 1              (record after)
RETURN  ans
```

stages.title: Reference C++
Edge cases and complexity
stages.body:
✍️ O(n) average time, O(n) space.
✍️ Without the {0: 1} seed, [3] with k = 3 returns 0.
✍️ Recording before querying with k = 0 counts each position as a zero-length subarray.

stages.title: Carry forward
stages.body:
✍️ Subarray sum = k (or divisible by k, or balanced counts) → prefix sum + hash map.
✍️ It is Two Sum where the "values" are prefix sums: store what you have seen, look up run − k.
✍️ Negatives allowed → do not use a sliding window.

stages.title: Interview follow-ups
stages.body:
- *Longest subarray with sum k.* Map prefix → first index, seed {0: −1} ([[ps-prefix-sum-hashmap#variations]]).
- *Sum divisible by k.* Key by `run mod k`, normalised ([[ps-modular-prefix]]).
- *All values positive?* Then a sliding window also works in O(1) space.

siblings.title: Subarray Sums Divisible by K
siblings.maps: Same counting map, but keyed by the prefix sum's remainder mod k.

stages.title: Analyse
stages.body: ✍️ Count subarrays whose sum is divisible by k. Values can be negative.

stages.title: Brainstorm
stages.body: ✍️ sum(i..j) divisible ⇔ pre[j+1] ≡ pre[i] (mod k). Count equal remainders with an array of size k seeded with count[0] = 1. Normalise negative remainders.

stages.title: Algorithm in words
stages.body: ✍️ For each element: update the running remainder; add how many earlier prefixes had the same remainder; record it.

stages.title: Pseudocode
stages.body:
```
cnt[k] = 0; cnt[0] = 1; run = 0; ans = 0
for x in a:
    run = ((run + x) % k + k) % k
    ans += cnt[run]; cnt[run]++
```

stages.title: Reference C++
Quick theory
stages.body: ✍️ Equal remainders bound a divisible subarray ([[ps-modular-prefix#idea]]); C++ `%` can be negative ([[ps-modular-prefix#negative-mod]]).

siblings.title: Contiguous Array
siblings.maps: Turn 0 into −1; equal 0s and 1s means sum 0; find the longest such subarray with a first-index map.

stages.title: Analyse
stages.body: ✍️ Longest subarray of a binary array with equally many 0s and 1s.

stages.title: Brainstorm
stages.body: ✍️ Map 0 → −1. Then "equal counts" = "sum 0". Longest subarray with sum 0: two equal prefix sums; store the **first** index of each prefix value, seed {0: −1}.

stages.title: Algorithm in words
stages.body: ✍️ Running sum with ±1; if this sum was seen, length = i − first[sum]; otherwise record first[sum] = i.

stages.title: Pseudocode
Reference C++
Quick theory
stages.body: ✍️ "Longest" → store the **first** occurrence (never overwrite); "count" → store counts ([[ps-prefix-sum-hashmap#variations]]).

siblings.title: Binary Subarrays With Sum
siblings.maps: Exactly Subarray Sum Equals K on a 0/1 array (the window alternative is atMost(goal) − atMost(goal−1)).

stages.title: Analyse
stages.body: ✍️ Count subarrays of a binary array with sum equal to goal.

stages.title: Brainstorm
stages.body: ✍️ Prefix + count map, identical template. Alternative: because values are ≥ 0, sliding windows work with the at-most trick ([[sw-at-most-k-trick#idea]]).

stages.title: Algorithm in words
stages.body: ✍️ Running sum; add cnt[run − goal]; record run.

stages.title: Pseudocode
stages.body:
```
cnt = {0:1}; run = 0; ans = 0
for x in a: run += x; ans += cnt[run-goal]; cnt[run]++
```

stages.title: Reference C++
Quick theory
stages.body: ✍️ When prefix values are small and non-negative, an array replaces the hash map ([[cpp-container-choice#rule]]).
